To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Latin America and East Asian countries had different responses to the return of private capital in the 1991-94 period because of the difference in the external debt ceilings in the late 1970s and early 1980s.
Latin America's lower debt ceiling prior to the 1990 capital return and a higher propensity to import consumption goods were important determinants of its larger current account deterioration.
Latin America's higher current account deficits after the return of private capital were due to a lower debt ceiling, while East Asia's were due to a higher ceiling.
